Nevada Commercial/ACA Appeals Department  
[Appeals address or fax number]

Re: Quinn Hayes  
Member ID: W991965754  
Reference number: POC-CFA5B97DE7-76391  
Denied service: Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy  
CPT: 29881

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial dated August 8, 2026, for the requested knee arthroscopy/meniscus surgery, CPT 29881. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. Please reverse the denial and authorize the surgery.

The clinical record supports medical necessity under the publicly available Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines—Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery, policy number MSK02-1125.1, effective November 15, 2025. The guideline states:

“Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirms the diagnosis or establishes its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention.”

This requirement is met. The patient has had 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. MRI performed on June 21, 2026, confirms a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.

The guideline also states:

“The anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms, including from delay or decreased access to services that may result (net benefit).”

The requested surgery has a favorable medical rationale because the displaced tear is causing mechanical locking, giving way, inability to squat or kneel, and limitation to level walking. Continued delay risks persistent mechanical symptoms and further functional limitation. The MRI shows preserved articular cartilage and only grade 1 Kellgren-Lawrence changes, supporting the conclusion that the primary problem is the displaced meniscal tear rather than advanced degenerative arthritis.

The guideline further states:

“Widely used treatment guidelines and/or current clinical literature and/or standards of medical practice should support that the recommended intervention offers the greatest net benefit among competing alternatives.”

Nonoperative treatment has already been attempted extensively and has not adequately relieved the condition:

- Supervised physical therapy emphasizing quadriceps strengthening and range of motion was completed for 16 weeks, from March 16, 2026, through July 6, 2026, with 16 visits documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAID treatment was used for six months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 20, 2026, produced only four weeks of partial relief.
- Rest has not relieved the symptoms.

Because the tear is displaced and associated with mechanical locking, the record supports operative treatment as the next medically appropriate intervention after failed conservative care.

The guideline also states:

“There exists a reasonable likelihood that the intervention will change management and/or lead to an improved outcome for the patient.”

That requirement is met. Treating the displaced medial-meniscus tear is reasonably expected to reduce locking and pain and improve walking, range of motion, and the ability to perform activities such as squatting and kneeling.

The patient has no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. The patient is a nonsmoker and has a BMI of 29. These facts do not identify a clinical barrier to surgery. The treating orthopedic surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, has evaluated the patient and requested the procedure.

The guideline states:

“Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider’s clinical intent.”

The prior-authorization packet contains the relevant documentation, including the MRI report, examination findings, physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, functional limitations, and the surgeon’s request.

For these reasons, I request that Anthem overturn the denial and approve CPT 29881. If Anthem relied on a different Anthem medical policy, a proprietary MCG guideline, or other plan-specific criteria rather than the publicly available Carelon guideline, please provide the exact criteria used in this determination, including the applicable document title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific unmet criterion. Please also identify the clinical information that Anthem believes is missing or insufficient and allow the treating surgeon an opportunity for peer-to-peer review.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Quinn Hayes
